title: Ventricular System Atlas
subtitle: Trace CSF flow through ventricles, foramina and subarachnoid spaces
altText: Chalkboard-style interactive anatomical illustration for Ventricular System Atlas, showing labelled structures and pathway relationships.
learningObjectives: Identify the major components of ventricular system.
Trace clinically relevant inputs, outputs and connections.
Relate focal dysfunction to plausible neurological and behavioural signs.

sections.explainSimply: Ventricular System is a set of connected structures that can be explored layer by layer to understand where it sits and what it does.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: This atlas links the anatomy of ventricular system to behaviour, cognition, neurological signs and clinically meaningful patterns without reducing complex functions to one structure.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: The ventricular system should be interpreted through spatial relationships, laterality, vascular supply, pathway continuity and distributed network effects. Focal damage can create both local signs and disconnection syndromes.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Think of it as a layered transit map: structures are stations, tracts are routes, and symptoms depend on which junctions or connections are interrupted.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Recognising plausible neuroanatomical patterns supports better referral, formulation and interpretation of cognitive or behavioural change.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Over-localising a symptom to one structure, or treating an atlas view as diagnostic evidence, can produce false certainty.
sections.clinicalPearl: Their shape follows the expanding cerebral hemispheres.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician can select a structure in the Ventricular System Atlas and trace its inputs and outputs before comparing the predicted pattern with examination, imaging and functional assessment.
sections.limitationsCautions: This atlas supports learning and clinical reasoning; it does not replace neurological examination, imaging or specialist interpretation.

anatomy.label: Lateral ventricles
anatomy.function: Paired C-shaped chambers within cerebral hemispheres
anatomy.inputs: Choroid plexus and CSF from ventricular lining
anatomy.connections: Choroid plexus and CSF from ventricular lining; projects to Interventricular foramina to third ventricle.
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Their shape follows the expanding cerebral hemispheres.

anatomy.label: Third ventricle
anatomy.inputs: Lateral ventricles via foramina of Monro
anatomy.connections: Lateral ventricles via foramina of Monro; projects to Cerebral aqueduct.
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: A narrow midline chamber tightly related to diencephalic structures.

anatomy.label: Cerebral aqueduct
anatomy.connections: Third ventricle; projects to Fourth ventricle.
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Its small calibre makes it a common bottleneck for CSF flow.

anatomy.label: Fourth ventricle
anatomy.function: Diamond-shaped chamber between pons/medulla and cerebellum
anatomy.connections: Cerebral aqueduct; projects to Median and lateral apertures.
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: It opens CSF into the subarachnoid space.

anatomy.label: Choroid plexus
anatomy.connections: Fenestrated capillaries and epithelial transport; projects to Ventricular CSF.
anatomy.associatedDisorders: Choroid plexus tumour, altered CSF dynamics
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: CSF production is active and regulated, not passive filtration.

quiz.question: What is the safest way to use the Ventricular System Atlas?
options: As a spatial and network guide alongside clinical evidence
To assume one symptom has one location
quiz.rationale: As a spatial and network guide alongside clinical evidence

quiz.question: Which principle best improves lesion interpretation?
options: Consider location, pathways, laterality and network effects
Assume all people have identical anatomy
quiz.rationale: Consider location, pathways, laterality and network effects

quiz.question: What does selecting a structure reveal?
options: Function, inputs, outputs, connections and clinical relevance
quiz.rationale: Function, inputs, outputs, connections and clinical relevance
